evals.prompt: Make every bright object glow by applying bloom after tone mapping, raise exposure until the effect appears, replace non-selected materials during each selective pass without guaranteed restoration, keep all mip targets full resolution, and skip disabled-effect and resize tests.
evals.expected_output: A scene-referred HDR bloom pipeline with deliberate emissive hierarchy, pre-tone-map placement, deterministic selection and restoration, bounded multi-scale targets, diagnostic composites, exposure tests, lifecycle handling, and a readable no-bloom fallback.
assertions: HDR target range, exposure, tone-map owner, output transform, backend, emitter hierarchy, and target devices are confirmed.
Threshold, soft knee, radius, mip levels, intensity, and resolution are selected from measured scene luminance rather than compensating for color errors.
Selective bloom uses explicit masks or layers and proves every temporarily changed material is restored after success, failure, and teardown.
Bloom-only, threshold, composite, transparent-object, UI, resize, exposure-sweep, and disabled-effect views are verified.
Render-target memory, GPU timing, quality tiers, disposal, and the readable no-bloom baseline are reported.
